attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack essay. Nearby book quotes are marked as quotes, but this sentence is his own.

semantics.note: Saying it is 'preposterous to think' a system will acquire this knowledge is a firm conditional denial, not a hedge. The chess antecedent and the 'just from statistical analysis of big data' limit are both kept. The claim is partly an argument, but it is fair to treat it as a conditional forecast with no deadline.

contract.note: The readings of 'robust model', 'can't induce' and 'all it needs to know' are ordinary and not stretched. The contract fairly requires both sides of a counterexample to be shown in the same system. In practice the claim can only be contradicted, never confirmed. 'Condition met' rests on chess-specific models, not general LLMs.

evidence.note: Preprint dated Feb 2026 showing that chess-trained transformers fail on chess rules when positions are out of distribution. This bears on the antecedent only, and only for narrow chess models. It says nothing about the outcome.
2021/2022 study showing that transformers can learn to predict legal chess moves fairly well. It cautions against treating chess failure as universal. It does not test broader reasoning.
TIME temporal-reasoning benchmark, dated Oct 2025. It does not test chess rules, so it gives no matched evidence on the same system.
XFinBench, dated Aug 2025: the best model still trails human experts on finance tasks. It does not test chess, so it cannot show both sides of the conditional.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline. None of the evidence shows a single system that fails on chess rules yet reasons reliably about time, finance, shopping and everyday change from statistical training alone, so nothing meets the contradiction condition. Ongoing failures cannot confirm a claim with no end date. The antecedent is shown only for chess-specific models. The evidence available by the cutoff does not settle the claim.
